evidence.claim: FixedTermLoanHooks.onQueueWithdrawal gates on block.timestamp rather than the batch expiry, forcing lenders to wait an extra withdrawalBatchDuration before withdrawing.
evidence.support_reason: onQueueWithdrawal reverts while fixedTermEndTime > block.timestamp (line 857), ignoring the expiry argument. The expiry is set to block.timestamp + withdrawalBatchDuration in _queueWithdrawal (WildcatMarketWithdrawals.sol:95-96), and executeWithdrawal reverts until expiry (line 239). So a lender queuing at term end must wait the batch duration before executing.
preconditions: Market uses FixedTermLoanHooks with a nonzero withdrawalBatchDuration

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the extra wait is a defect rather than intended fixed-term semantics (the term is a minimum lockup; the batch duration is the standard withdrawal cycle applied to all markets).
missing_evidence.why: The claim's impact is a timing inconvenience; without evidence that the design intends withdrawal to be executable at term end (not merely queueable), the effect does not establish a security impact or severity.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A cited spec/doc statement or code invariant shows withdrawals should be executable at fixedTermEndTime, or a concrete loss (e.g., interest/penalty accrual or blocked exit) is shown.
